faqs.question: How do I write Navratri wishes with a name without any app?
faqs.answer: Pick a wish with a blank, such as "___, may Maa Durga keep your home full of light this Navratri", and type the person's name into the blank before you send it. It needs no app and no upload, and works in any chat. Lead with the name, because the first words are what the notification preview shows.

faqs.question: What are the no-cost ways to add a name and photo to a Navratri wish online?
faqs.answer: The usual routes are a name-on-image generator site, your phone's built-in photo editor, or a personalised link page. The generator is fastest but uploads the photo to a server you cannot inspect; the phone editor keeps it on your device; a link page uploads it but can be password-protected.

faqs.question: Should I ask before putting a friend's face on a Navratri greeting?
faqs.answer: It is a risk you take on their behalf. Research summarised in Communications of the ACM (2018) found deleted photo URLs stayed reachable for 3 to over 30 days depending on the platform, and you cannot see how a free generator stores uploads. Ask first, or use a photo of yourself.

faqs.question: Does WhatsApp remove location data from photos I send?
faqs.answer: In normal chat mode, yes: a 2025 forensic study found WhatsApp image transfers strip Exif data including GPS through compression. Sending the same photo as a document kept every Exif field, as did email and USB. The original in your gallery still carries it.

faqs.question: Where should the name go in a Navratri message?
faqs.answer: First, in most cases. 48.3% of SubhSandesh's shared pages are opened on a phone, and a phone shows only the opening words in a notification. For elders, use "ji" or the relationship word, such as Nani or Mausi, instead of a first name.

faqs.question: Can I send a personalised Navratri wish to a WhatsApp group?
faqs.answer: Not with a single name slot. For a group or a broadcast list, send a well-written wish with no name; a template carrying the wrong name is worse than none. Save the named version for the handful of people you message one to one.

faqs.question: What should I write in a Navratri wish for my boss with their name?
faqs.answer: Keep it short and formal, with no photo: "Dear ___, wishing you and your family a peaceful Navratri and a bright Vijayadashami on ___. Warm regards, ___." Fill in their name, your local Dussehra date (20 October 2026 in Delhi, 21 October in Bengal and Mysuru; 9 October 2027) and your own name.

faqs.question: Is the Be My Dandiya Partner page a Navratri greeting card?
faqs.answer: No. It is a one-to-one dandiya invitation for a partner, a crush or a best friend as garba buddy, with nine short lines, up to six photos and the night's details. It is the wrong tool for wishing family, an office or a society group, and its interface is in English.

faqs.question: When is Navratri in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Sharad Navratri runs from 11 to 19 October 2026, with Dussehra on Tuesday 20 October, according to Drik Panchang's New Delhi calendar; Bengal and Mysuru mark Dussehra on Wednesday 21 October. In 2027 it runs from 30 September to 8 October, with Dussehra on 9 October.

faqs.question: Can I password-protect a personalised Navratri page?
faqs.answer: On SubhSandesh, yes: a password is optional when you publish, and 38.5% of creators password-protect their page before sharing it. A name-on-image picture cannot be locked once it is sent, because anyone can forward the file.

faqs.question: Do I need consent to use someone's photo in a Navratri greeting in India?
faqs.answer: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 does not apply to personal data an individual processes for a personal or domestic purpose, which covers making a greeting. Its duties do apply to the website that processes the photo. Asking the person first is still the decent default; this is not legal advice.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Navratri Wishes With Name: Templates, Photos and What You Upload

The simplest way to send Navratri wishes with name is a text template with a blank you fill in yourself: free, no upload, and it works in any chat app. On SubhSandesh, 38.5% of creators password-protect a page before sharing it, and 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so add a photo only when you know where it goes, and put the name in the first few words. Below are 12 original wishes with a name slot, four ways to add a name and photo compared on cost and privacy, and what happens to someone's face when you upload it to a free generator.

## What does "Navratri wishes with name" mean?

A Navratri wish with name is a festival greeting that carries the recipient's name in the text or printed on the image, and often their photo too. It replaces "Happy Navratri to you and your family" with a line written for one person.

The wishes in this post fit both Sharad Navratri windows: 11 to 19 October 2026, with Dussehra on 20 October (21 October in Bengal and Mysuru), and 30 September to 8 October 2027, with Dussehra on 9 October 2027, per [Drik Panchang's New Delhi calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/navratri/ashwin-shardiya-navratri-dates.html?geoname-id=1261481&year=2026). Hindi wording and a romantic line for each night are separate guides in this series; this one is about putting a name and a picture on whatever wish you choose.

Why bother with the name at all? A 2026 EEG study of 38 adults [in Brain Sciences](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13297153) found a person's own name produced a P300 response of 3.95 μV against 1.77 μV for a plain tone, and lit up 12 brain clusters against 7. Those were spoken names in a lab, not a WhatsApp card: a reason the name catches attention, not proof of a warmer reply.

## 12 Navratri wishes with a name slot, by who you're sending to

Each group gives the wish, who it suits and where the name goes. Replace every ___ with a name, a night number or a date, and lead with the name where you can: the opening words are what a notification preview shows.

### 1. For parents, grandparents and elders

1. "___, may Maa Shailputri keep you as steady as the mountain she is named for. Happy Navratri from all of us."
2. "___ ji, your blessings carried me through every exam season. This Navratri, may Maa Durga return them a hundred times over."

Suits: anyone you touch feet for. Name position: first, with "ji" or the relationship word ("Nani", "Mausi") rather than a first name.

### 2. For family you're close to

3. "Nine nights, nine forms of Maa, and one wish for you, ___: a home where the diya never runs short of ghee."
4. "___, may this Navratri burn off whatever has been sitting heavy on you. Maa Kalaratri is good at exactly that."

Suits: siblings, cousins, the aunt who sends you forwards. Name position: first or middle.

### 3. For friends and your garba group

5. "___, I'm saving you a spot in the second circle from the centre. May Maa keep your feet tireless and your phone charged till midnight."
6. "To ___, who knows every step and still asks for one more practice round: Jai Mata Di, see you on night ___."

Suits: the friend you dance with. Wish 6 has two slots, a name and a night number.

### 4. For a colleague, client or boss

7. "Dear ___, wishing you and your family a peaceful Navratri and a bright Vijayadashami on ___. Warm regards, ___."
8. "___, may the nine days bring you clear deadlines and quieter evenings. Happy Navratri."

Suits: anyone you would email rather than voice-note. Fill your local Dussehra date (20 October 2026 in Delhi, 9 October 2027) and sign your own name; no photo.

### 5. For a partner, kept light

9. "___, of all nine colours this week, you're still my favourite one."
10. "___, Maa Durga fought for nine nights. I'm only asking you for one dance."

Suits: someone you're dating. Name position: first, always.

### 6. For someone far away this Navratri

11. "___, the aarti here sounds the same without you, but the prasad tastes less sweet. Happy Navratri from ___."
12. "It's night ___ here, ___. I lit one extra diya and decided it's yours."

Suits: a child at college, a parent abroad, a friend who moved cities. The second slot (your city, or the night) is the detail that makes it personal.

## Four ways to add a name and photo, compared

The table compares four methods on cost, whether the other person's photo leaves your phone, and whether you control who opens the result. The last column is SubhSandesh's own measurement where one exists.

| Method | Cost | Their photo leaves your phone? | Can you lock it? | SubhSandesh data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain text wish you type yourself (no SubhSandesh product) | ₹0, nothing to buy | No photo used | No; it sits in the chat | 48.3% of shared pages open on a phone, so short text suits it |
| Name-on-image generator site | ₹0 on the no-signup versions | Yes, uploaded to a server you cannot inspect | No; the image can be forwarded freely | None |
| Phone or desktop design editor | ₹0 with your phone's built-in editor | On-device editors: no. Cloud editors: yes | No; you export an image | None |
| Personalised link page, e.g. a dandiya invitation | Not priced in this post | Yes, uploaded to the page's host | Yes, optional password | 38.5% of creators password-protect; 90.9% of started pages get published |

The takeaway: the text template is the only option with no upload, and the link page the only one with a lock. A generator site is fastest for a name on a picture, and the one where you know least about what happens next.

## Is it safe to upload someone's photo to a name generator?

It is safe enough for your own face; for someone else's, you are taking the risk on their behalf. Three things to know first.

First, a photo can carry more than a face. A 2025 forensic study of image transfer methods by [Nishchal Soni in Perspectives in Legal and Forensic Sciences](https://www.sciepublish.com/index/article/view_full_text/id/567) found that sending through WhatsApp, Instagram or Snapchat chat strips Exif data including GPS location, while WhatsApp document mode, email and USB kept every field. The original file in your gallery still has it; whether a free generator removes it is something you cannot see from outside.

Second, deletion is slower than people assume. [Such and Criado's 2018 review in Communications of the ACM](https://kclpure.kcl.ac.uk/ws/files/82576549/multi_party_privacy_management.pdf) reports earlier measurements in which a deleted photo's URL stayed reachable for 3 days on Instagram, 7 on Facebook, 14 on Flickr and over 30 on MySpace and Tumblr. The same paper makes the point this whole section rests on: privacy is also about what other people disclose about you.

Third, the law draws a line between you and the website. India's [Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/06/2bf1f0e9f04e6fb4f8fef35e82c42aa5.pdf) defines personal data as any data about an identifiable individual, so a face qualifies, but it does not apply to data an individual processes for a personal or domestic purpose, which covers you making a greeting. Its duties fall on the company that decides how that data is processed: the site you upload to, so read its privacy page first.

A practical rule: use your own photo or one of the two of you, and ask before using anyone else's. Never upload a child's photo to a site whose name you didn't know yesterday.

## When a personalised page beats an image

A picture with a name on it is finished the moment you send it. A link page holds several photos and a longer note, can be locked, and can be edited after sending.

Timing matters too. SubhSandesh has no Navratri build data yet; in its nearest festival measurement, Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89 pages, a different, one-day festival), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself and the median lead time was zero days. Most people personalise on the day, so pick a method you can finish in one sitting.

If the person you want to wish is the one you want beside you in the circle, the [Be My Dandiya Partner invitation](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) is built for that. You add their name and yours, nine short lines (one for each night of Navratri), up to six photos, and the night's date, time, venue and dress code. It opens in any phone or laptop browser with no app or account, can be password-protected at publish, and ends with a 1080×1920 Dandiya Pass sized for an Instagram Story.

Be clear about what it is: a one-to-one dandiya invitation for your love, your crush or a best friend as garba buddy, not a general greeting card. It is the wrong tool for wishing your whole family, your society group or your office, and its pages are in English.

If your far-away person matters more than the garba plan, an [I miss you page](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits a long-distance greeting better. The [full SubhSandesh template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) covers other occasions.

## When a name-and-photo wish is the wrong choice

A name slot does not scale. Wishing 150 contacts, a good wish with no name beats a template carrying the wrong one, an easy slip on the fortieth copy-paste.

Some people are private about their photos. A colleague, a new in-law or anyone whose display picture is blank would rather get text. And 48.3% of shared pages open on a phone, so roughly half open elsewhere; an elder with no smartphone would rather get a call.

And a link page loses to a plain image when the recipient never taps unfamiliar links, which is a sensible habit. Send the text wish first and the link second, with a line saying what it is.

- Duan F. et al., "Enhanced Neural Responses to Self-Name Stimuli…", Brain Sciences 16(6):608, 2 June 2026.
- Such J. and Criado N., "Multiparty Privacy in Social Media", Communications of the ACM 61(8), August 2018.
- Soni N., "Forensic Value of Exif Data…", Perspectives in Legal and Forensic Sciences, 18 June 2025.
- The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (No. 22 of 2023), Gazette of India, 11 August 2023.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the incumbents: of the 9 US-served (WebSearch) results, 8 are weak, undated or stale wish lists, and none of the pages read offers a name slot, compares ways to add a name and photo, or says what happens to an uploaded face; this post does all three with first-party numbers (38.5% password, 48.3% phone) and fetched evidence on Exif stripping, deletion lag and the DPDP Act. The novelty claim rests on 3 of the top 5 read in full: hindutone (502) was never read beyond its snippet. What it cannot overcome: subhsandesh.in's domain authority against hindupad and hindutone, India-served positions were not measured, demand is modest (autocomplete rank 4), the self-name EEG study is about heard names rather than written ones, and the Exif source is from a young OA publisher. It will not outrank hindupad soon; ranking, if it comes, takes months.
